name: Woodstock
hook: Three days of peace, music and mud on a New York farm in August 1969.

facts.label: Bethel, New York
facts.statement: The festival ran August 15-18, 1969 on Max Yasgur's farm in Bethel, Sullivan County, New York — not in Woodstock — drawing over 300,000.

facts.label: Jimi Hendrix
facts.statement: Jimi Hendrix played a searing "Star-Spangled Banner" at Woodstock; he told Dick Cavett, "I'm American, so I played it."

facts.label: Richie Havens
facts.statement: Richie Havens opened the festival and, called back for so many encores he ran out of material, improvised "Freedom."

facts.label: the 1970 documentary
facts.statement: The 1970 documentary Woodstock includes Max Yasgur's speech; Martin Scorsese worked on it as an assistant director and supervising editor.

facts.label: The Who
facts.statement: The Who played Woodstock; Pete Townshend said the "desolation" there inspired "Baba O'Riley."

facts.label: granola
facts.statement: Thousands of cups of granola were passed down from the stage to feed the huge crowd.

facts.label: Filippini's Pond
facts.statement: At Woodstock, concertgoers shed their clothes and inhibitions by skinny-dipping in Filippini's Pond.
